intro: NHS Pharmacy First lets our pharmacists assess and treat seven common conditions — including prescribing medicines where appropriate — without you needing to see a GP first. For most of these conditions you can simply walk in and ask.

conditions.note: We'll check for signs of infection and can prescribe antibiotics if they're needed.

conditions.plainName: a crusty, weeping skin infection, often around the nose and mouth
conditions.note: Impetigo spreads easily between family members and at school or nursery — early treatment helps stop that.

conditions.plainName: a bite that has become red, hot or swollen
conditions.note: We'll look at the bite and can treat straightforward infections on the spot.

conditions.plainName: a painful, blistering rash, usually on one side of the body
conditions.note: Shingles treatment works best started early, so don't wait if you suspect it — come straight in.

conditions.plainName: a sinus infection, with facial pain or a blocked, thick-mucus nose
conditions.note: Most sinusitis clears on its own, but we can advise or treat if it's severe or not improving.
We'll check for signs that need antibiotics rather than just time and fluids.

conditions.plainName: a bladder infection with stinging, urgency or needing to go often
conditions.note: A quick, private conversation and, where appropriate, a dipstick test in the consultation room.

howItWorks.title: Ask at the counter, or arrive by referral
howItWorks.copy: Walk in and tell any member of the team what's wrong — no booking needed. Your GP practice or NHS 111 can also refer you straight to us if they think Pharmacy First is the right route.

howItWorks.title: A short, private consultation
howItWorks.copy: One of our pharmacists takes you into the consultation room, asks about your symptoms and, where needed, does a simple examination or test — the same confidentiality as a GP appointment.

howItWorks.title: Treatment, advice, or a safety-net referral
howItWorks.copy: Most people leave with treatment or clear advice on the same visit. If your symptoms need more than we can offer, we'll refer you on — to your GP, an urgent care service, or 999 if it's serious.

referralRoutes: Walk in and ask at the counter — no appointment or referral needed for most people
Referral from Willowbrook Surgery or another local GP practice
Referral from NHS 111, online or by phone
freeOnNhsCopy: NHS Pharmacy First is free on the NHS. There's nothing to pay for the consultation, and any medicine we prescribe under the service is also free of charge — the same as an NHS prescription exemption, but without the paperwork.
reviewedPathwaysNote: The seven Pharmacy First clinical pathways shown here were last reviewed against national guidance in October 2025.
